Tin
tin
noun
Hebrew bedil (H913) — the soft white metal (Sn), alloyed with copper to make bronze; mentioned among the metals refined out of dross (Num 31:22; Isa 1:25; Ezek 22:18-20), and as the supply Tyre received from Tarshish (Ezek 27:12).

📖 Biblical Definition

Tin in biblical theology appears mostly in the context of REFINING — separated as dross from the more precious metals in the refiner's fire. Isaiah 1:25 promises God's purification of Israel: "I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin." Ezekiel develops the metaphor at length (Ezek 22:18-20): Israel has become to God "as dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are even the dross of silver." The refiner heats the alloy to melt and separate the impurities; tin (along with lead, brass, iron) is what the refiner's fire RELEASES the silver from. So tin in Scripture pictures what God burns away from His people — the dross of mixed loyalties, of compromised faith, of impurities accumulated through generations. Numbers 31:22 lists tin among the metals that must "go through the fire" when the Israelites returned from the war with Midian — the spoils of war required ritual purification by fire because they had been used in idolatry. Tin from Tarshish (Ezek 27:12) was a major trade commodity reaching Tyre — likely from Cornwall (Britain) or northern Spain. The tin trade is one of the earliest documented sea-borne metal trades in history, and Tarshish ships were famous for it. Tin's biblical lesson: not every metal in the alloy gets to stay. God refines His people; the dross — tin, lead, brass, iron — burns away so that the silver remains.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A soft white metal (Sn), alloyed with copper to make bronze; in Scripture mostly the metaphor of dross burned away by the refiner's fire.

expand to see more

TIN, noun. A soft, malleable, silvery-white metal (Sn), used since antiquity to alloy with copper for bronze. Major ancient source: the tin mines of Cornwall (Britain), traded via Phoenician/Tarshish ships.

In Scripture, listed among metals refined out of dross (Num 31:22; Isa 1:25; Ezek 22:18-20); the trade goods Tarshish supplied to Tyre (Ezek 27:12); the impurity God promises to purge from His people.

📖 Key Scripture

Isaiah 1:25 — "And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin."

Ezekiel 22:18-19 — "Son of man, the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are even the dross of silver. Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye are all become dross, behold, therefore I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem."

Numbers 31:22 — "Only the gold, and the silver, the brass, the iron, the tin, and the lead, Every thing that may abide the fire, ye shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be clean."

Ezekiel 27:12 — "Tarshish was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of all kind of riches; with silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded in thy fairs."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Tin is corrupted when the refiner's-fire theology of Isaiah 1:25 and Ezekiel 22:18-20 is severed from the personal application (God refining HIS people, not just ancient Israel), or when the historical Tarshish-tin trade is mythologized rather than received as the real material economy God's people inhabited.

expand to see more

Refiner's-fire severance. Isaiah 1:25 and Ezekiel 22:18-20 are not just historical descriptions of God's judgment on ancient Israel; they describe God's permanent refining work on His people. Peter applies the same fire-refining language to all believers (1 Pet 1:7) — "the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire." The tin in you — the alloyed mix of compromised loyalty, impure motive, divided affection — is what God promises to purge. To strip the personal application is to imagine yourself outside the furnace.

Historical-trade mythologizing. The Tarshish-tin trade was historically real: Phoenician/Tarshish ships sailed from the eastern Mediterranean to the British Isles for Cornish tin centuries before Christ. Ezekiel 27:12 is accurate ancient economic history. Some commentators treat this as legendary or symbolic; the archaeological record supports it. God's people inhabit a real material economy, and the Bible accurately describes it.
